clauses.text:
By virtue of and pursuant to the au­
thority vested in me by the Career Com­
pensation Act of 1949, approved October 
12, 1949, the existing regulations pre­
scribed by Executive orders pursuant to 
the authority contained in the Pay Re­
adjustment Act of 1942 of June 16, 1942, 
as amended, and existing departmental 
regulations and determinations pre­
scribed or made pursuant to the author­
ity contained in such act or in such 
Executive orders are hereby adopted 
and prescribed, so far as applicable and 
appropriate, as regulations required or 
authorized to be prescribed by the Presi­
dent under Titles II, III, and V of the said 
Career Compensation Act of 1949.
This order shall take effect on October 
1, 1949, and shall cease to be effective 
on January 31, 1950.

versions.research_rationale:
Executive Order 10084 (14 FR 6245 (Federal Register of October 14, 1949)) concerns the order that adopts, as regulations under Titles II, III and V of the Career Compensation Act of 1949, the existing pay regulations, and fixes how long that adoption lasts. Executive Order 10084 was signed October 12, 1949 and takes effect October 1, 1949. Its sole paragraph adopts and prescribes the existing regulations under the Pay Readjustment Act of 1942, and existing departmental regulations and determinations, so far as applicable and appropriate, as regulations under Titles II, III and V of the Act, and its last sentence reads “This order shall take effect on October 1, 1949, and shall cease to be effective on January 31, 1950”. Sunset text by instrument: Executive Order 10084 (October 12, 1949): the order shall cease to be effective on January 31, 1950. Executive Order 10098 (signed January 25, 1950): the last paragraph restated, ceasing March 31, 1950. Executive Order 10118 (signed March 27, 1950): last paragraph restated, ceasing March 31, 1950 except that, to the extent it adopts regulations under sections 201(e), 204, 206, 302 and 501(d) of the Career Compensation Act of 1949, it continues until June 30, 1950. Executive Order 10136 (signed June 30, 1950, effective July 1, 1950): sections 201(e), 204, 206 and 501(d) continue until August 31, 1950 and section 302 until September 30, 1950. Executive Order 10158 (signed August 31, 1950, effective September 1, 1950): sections 206 and 302 continue until October 31, 1950. Executive Order 10174 (signed October 23, 1950, effective November 1, 1950): section 302 continues until January 31, 1951. Each amendment takes effect the day after the earlier date it extends ends, so the dates are read inclusively and leave no gap. The last held instrument is Executive Order 10174 (15 FR 7165 (Federal Register of October 26, 1950)), which continues the order, to the extent it adopts regulations under section 302 of the Act, “until January 31, 1951”. On 2026-10-14 the clause is terminated at that last sunset, January 31, 1951, inclusive; the exclusive reading would end it when that day begins. The dossier's later-event chain and the held-text search for citations of Executive Order No. 10084 (searched also with a trailing footnote digit) show no later instrument after Executive Order 10174: the Federal Register disposition-note search lists the five amendments named above, and the U.S. Code and eCFR citation searches report no hit. A later extension that the held corpus lacks is not excluded, which is the usual limit of a bounded search and is disclosed.

Sunset text by instrument: Executive Order 10084 (October 12, 1949): the order shall cease to be effective on January 31, 1950. Executive Order 10098 (signed January 25, 1950): the last paragraph restated, ceasing March 31, 1950. Executive Order 10118 (signed March 27, 1950): last paragraph restated, ceasing March 31, 1950 except that, to the extent it adopts regulations under sections 201(e), 204, 206, 302 and 501(d) of the Career Compensation Act of 1949, it continues until June 30, 1950. Executive Order 10136 (signed June 30, 1950, effective July 1, 1950): sections 201(e), 204, 206 and 501(d) continue until August 31, 1950 and section 302 until September 30, 1950. Executive Order 10158 (signed August 31, 1950, effective September 1, 1950): sections 206 and 302 continue until October 31, 1950. Executive Order 10174 (signed October 23, 1950, effective November 1, 1950): section 302 continues until January 31, 1951. Each amendment takes effect the day after the earlier date it extends ends, so the dates are read inclusively and leave no gap. No instrument ends the parent order before January 31, 1951, and no end on a date between amendments is shown, because each amendment takes effect the day after the preceding date.","independent_command_check":"The clause has one function, which is to fix the duration of the adoption of regulations in Executive Order No. 10084, and has no separate command. The listed sections are separately sunsetted by the amendments, but the parent order as a whole ends when the last of them ends, which is the date recorded.","savings_check":"The order's text has no saving clause. Pay and allowances earned under the regulations while they were adopted are entitlements under the Career Compensation Act of 1949 and the regulations then in force; the held text creates no continuing duty after January 31, 1951, and the bounded searches found no later order continuing or restoring the adoption.","scope_check":"One operative paragraph (the adoption of regulations) whose closing sentence states the effective date and the original sunset; the dossier's single clause covers both."}
